children: Shares of Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) were in the green in opening trade on Friday after US defence major GE Aerospace delivered three F404-IN20 engines to the company in August for the LCA Tejas programme. The latest shipment takes cumulative Tejas Mk1A engine deliveries to 10 and comes as engine availability has been a key bottleneck for the programme.
Shares of HAL were trading at Rs 4,855 on the NSE at 9:19 am, up Rs 89.40 or 1.88% from the previous close.

Goldman Sachs has a 'Buy' call on HAL with a target price of Rs 5,870 per share. The brokerage said GE Aerospace shipped three F404 engines to HAL in August, compared with its estimate of two, taking cumulative engine deliveries to 10 from seven earlier.

Goldman Sachs said faster engine supplies are positive for HAL as availability of the F404 engines had been a key bottleneck for Tejas Mk1A deliveries. According to the brokerage's channel checks, 30 Mk1A airframes have already been assembled. Timely engine supplies should support HAL's delivery ramp-up and reduce execution risk, Goldman Sachs said.

GE Aerospace said on Thursday that it had shipped three F404-IN20 engines to HAL in August 2026. "We are proud to partner with HAL and the Indian Air Force to power India's indigenous fighter jets," the company said.

The latest shipment comes as HAL continues to receive engines for the Tejas Mk1A programme, which has faced delays due to supply-related constraints. Former HAL Chairman D.K. Sunil had said in April that GE had committed to supplying 20 F404 engines between June and December 2026. Engine availability has been a major factor behind delays in the production and delivery of the LCA Mk1A aircraft.
HAL officials had earlier said the contract with GE includes a provision for liquidated damages in case of delays in the delivery of F404 engines for the Light Combat Aircraft.
The Indian Air Force has placed an order with HAL for 180 LCA Mk1A fighter aircraft. GE Aerospace is contracted to supply 99 F404-IN20 engines under a Rs 5,375-crore contract signed in 2021.

GE Aerospace had earlier completed its commitment to HAL in 2016, delivering 65 F404-IN20 engines for the original Tejas LCA programme. With no additional engine orders at the time, production of the F404-IN20 was subsequently shut down.

The production line was restarted after HAL placed the additional order for 99 F404-IN20 engines in 2021. GE Aerospace also re-engaged its global supply chain to resume production after the engine line had remained dormant for five years.

The F404-IN20 is a version specifically developed for India's single-engine fighter. According to GE Aerospace, it delivers the highest thrust in the F404 engine family and incorporates a higher-flow fan, single-crystal turbine blades and other specialised components.

title: HAL shares jump nearly 2% as GE delivers 3 Tejas engines; Goldman Sachs stays bullish
